explanation: Solving a polynomial inequality is just reading off WHERE the graph is above (or below) the x-axis. The roots split the number line into intervals, and inside each interval the polynomial keeps one sign — so you only need to test a single point per interval. The green band along the axis marks every x that satisfies the chosen inequality; flip the direction slider to swap > 0 and < 0. Watch the moving test point report f(x) and whether it lands inside the solution set.
bullets: Roots cut the number line into intervals of constant sign.
Pick the intervals where the graph is on the correct side of the axis.
One test point per interval is enough — the sign can't change without a root.
